title: The first time offered for a message sent later follows the computer's clock, not India time
what: When the owner taps Later on a message card, the time filled in is worked out from the clock of his phone or laptop, while the rest of the app reads that time as India time. On a device set to another time zone the offered time is wrong, and it can even be in the past, so the card refuses it with 'Pick a time at least 5 minutes from now'.
expected: The time offered under Later is tomorrow 8 am or the next half hour in India time, whatever clock the device keeps, using the same India-time rule as the rest of the app.
who: owners whose device is not set to India time
how_often: every time Later is tapped on such a device
fix_line: Work out the offered time with the app's shared India-time helpers instead of the device clock

title: The assistant writes its own date words in three places instead of using the app's shared date rules
what: The History tab turns a time into India time with its own five-and-a-half-hour shift and its own month list, the credits sheet keeps another month list, and the weekday of a date has its own rule next to the shared one. Each copy can drift from the rest of the app (Hindi months, a changed format) without anyone noticing.
expected: One shared set of date and time rules used by the whole panel, so a change or fix lands everywhere at once.
how_often: not today; on the next date format change
fix_line: Use the shared date and time helpers in History, the credits sheet and the weekday rule

title: The AI Assistant can vanish for a few minutes after the owner switches gym while its credits were being loaded
what: Only one credits check can run at a time, whatever gym it is for. If the owner switches gym while the old gym's check is still running, the new gym's check is skipped and the old answer is then stored as the current one, so the assistant hides itself until the next check (up to 5 minutes, or when the tab is shown again).
expected: Switching gym starts the new gym's credits check at once, and a late answer for the old gym is thrown away.
who: owners with more than one gym
how_often: rare: only when switching gym during a slow check
fix_line: Keep the running check per gym and ignore an answer that comes back for a gym no longer open

title: Unused leftovers sit in the AI Assistant code, including a test reset no test ever calls
what: A 'forget everything, for tests' reset of who-may-see-the-assistant is never called because no test loads that file at all; an arrow icon and a message length limit are defined but used nowhere. Five assistant files, including the one that decides who sees the assistant, are imported by no unit test (the browser walk-through covers the main cases).
expected: No unused code; the who-may-see rule has a small test that uses the reset it was written for.
fix_line: Remove the unused pieces or add the small test the reset was meant for
